source_question: Based on the above information, is the following statement true, false, or uncertain? Adeline is intelligent.
formalization_prompt:
Read this logical world and question. Write ordinary SWI-Prolog source that you believe helps test one relevant hypothesis, plus one bare callable Prolog query to execute. The query is an API argument, not a console command: never include ?- or a trailing period. You may use normal facts, rules, helper predicates, and built-ins; do not call the shell, read files, use network, or add directives. This is an exploratory diagnostic, not a request for a final A/B/C answer.

Trusted Prolog capabilities can be inspected live with meta_signatures(Signatures) and meta_help(all, Documentation). Known callable signatures include audit_trace/2; audit_proof_tree/2; labelled_explanation/3; labelled_semantic_status/3; semantic_status/3; semantic_slice_status/3; finite_status/6; finite_sat_status/5. audit_proof_tree/2 returns a nested dependency tree only for a successful forward-Horn derivation; it never fabricates a proof for XOR, disjunction, negation, or quantifiers. Formulas accepted by the semantic helpers: atom(Name, Args), not(F), and(F,G), or(F,G), xor(F,G), implies(F,G), forall(var(Name,Type),F), exists(var(Name,Type),F). Explicit quantifier example: domain(person,[ada]). axiom(s1,forall(var(x,person),implies(calm(var(x)),ready(var(x))))). In the body, var(x) references the bound variable; x or 'X' alone is a constant. Every var(Name) reference must have an enclosing matching quantifier. Ordinary rule([calm(X)],ready(X)) implicitly quantifies its Prolog variable over person. Vacuous quantifiers and constants matching binder names are legal and reported by quantifier_audit; inspect their source text before changing them. Ordinary Prolog predicates may also be defined by your own source. This is a non-scoring executor-capability probe. Do not answer the English A/B/C question. The first declaration of your program MUST be exactly a top-level domain(person,[...]). declaration, never axiom(s0, domain(...)) and never any other wrapper. Then write a complete ordinary labelled Prolog formalization: every source sentence exactly once, with an s-ID from s1 through sN and its exact English in a preceding Prolog comment. Every source sentence MUST be an axiom/2 declaration. Do not write bare facts, normal Prolog clauses, sentence/2, person_member/1, or other helper predicates. Required fact form: axiom(s2, has_serpent_body(selah)). Required ordinary Horn rule form: axiom(s3, rule([has_wings(selah), has_serpent_body(selah)], rules_the_ocean(selah))). For complex non-Horn sentences use their labelled surface directly, such as axiom(s4, implies(...)), axiom(s5, not(...)), axiom(s6, or(...)), axiom(s7, xor(...)), or axiom(s8, and(...)). Preserve not/or/xor/and rather than deleting difficult sentences. Critical requirement: the source sentence whose ordinary Horn conclusion is `works_hard(adeline)` MUST use axiom(sN, rule([Premise,...], works_hard(adeline))), never implies(...), even if you use implies for other sentences. Your bare query must be exactly audit_proof_tree(works_hard(adeline), Result), with no ?- and no trailing period. This query asks only for the stated Horn subclaim `Adeline works hard.`, not for the English question. Do not use atom(Name,Args), directives, shell, files, network, semantic_status/3, labelled_explanation/3, finite_status/6, or finite_sat_status/5. Return JSON only: {"program":"...","query":"..."}. Return JSON only: {"program":"...","query":"..."}.

World:
If Adeline pursues her passion, then she will achieve success. Adeline is intelligent or dedicated. If Adeline sets goals, then she will work hard. If Adeline is dedicated, then she either has expertise or works hard (but not both). Adeline achieves success or has expertise. Adeline does not shape the opinions of others. Adeline sets goals. If Adeline achieves success, then she will gain recognition. If someone makes discoveries and publishes research, then they will have influence in their field. If Adeline is passionate, then she is dedicated and cares about others. Those who have influence in their field will shape the opinions of others. Briella sets goals. If someone gains recognition, then they will have influence in their field.

Question:
Based on the above information, is the following statement true, false, or uncertain? Adeline is intelligent.

formalization.program:
domain(person,[adeline,briella]).

% If Adeline pursues her passion, then she will achieve success.
axiom(s1, implies(pursues_passion(adeline), achieves_success(adeline))).

% Adeline is intelligent or dedicated.
axiom(s2, or(intelligent(adeline), dedicated(adeline))).

% If Adeline sets goals, then she will work hard.
axiom(s3, rule([set_goals(adeline)], works_hard(adeline))).

% If Adeline is dedicated, then she either has expertise or works hard (but not both).
axiom(s4, implies(dedicated(adeline), xor(has_expertise(adeline), works_hard(adeline)))).

% Adeline achieves success or has expertise.
axiom(s5, or(achieves_success(adeline), has_expertise(adeline))).

% Adeline does not shape the opinions of others.
axiom(s6, not(shapes_the_opinions_of_others(adeline))).

% Adeline sets goals.
axiom(s7, set_goals(adeline)).

% If Adeline achieves success, then she will gain recognition.
axiom(s8, implies(achieves_success(adeline), gains_recognition(adeline))).

% If someone makes discoveries and publishes research, then they will have influence in their field.
axiom(s9, forall(var(x,person), implies(and(makes_discoveries(var(x)), publishes_research(var(x))), has_influence_in_their_field(var(x))))).

% If Adeline is passionate, then she is dedicated and cares about others.
axiom(s10, implies(passionate(adeline), and(dedicated(adeline), cares_about_others(adeline)))).

% Those who have influence in their field will shape the opinions of others.
axiom(s11, rule([has_influence_in_their_field(X)], shapes_the_opinions_of_others(X))).

% Briella sets goals.
axiom(s12, set_goals(briella)).

% If someone gains recognition, then they will have influence in their field.
axiom(s13, rule([gains_recognition(X)], has_influence_in_their_field(X))).
